problem: Backup Bad Weather Day 2 (months/10-oct-zz-backup.md): the repaired Main Event step 5 now reads 'Line all four up beside her morning drawing at four o'clock, on the counter with Kreston in his high chair', but the Safety block it is governed by was left untouched and still reads 'Keep all four saucers on a high shelf: Kreston will eat what is on them.' The repairer also deviated from the sanctioned fix, which put the row at 'The Four Saucers, Looked At From Your Arms' and made step 5 hold each saucer and put it straight back.
fix: Amend the Safety sentence to match step 5: 'The saucers live on a high shelf and come down to the counter only while Kreston is strapped in his high chair, because he will eat what is on them.' Leave step 5 and the 4:15 row as they are.

problem: months/10-oct-w40.md: the new Safety sentence 'Kreston stays in the room with you and out of the hall while she is running it' is contradicted by Main Event step 6, 'Swap over. She counts and bangs, you run the hall, and you miss the stop once so she gets to call you out.' In step 6 the adult is in the hall, so the placement the Safety block promises leaves a 16-month-old in the room with a three-year-old banging a pan and no adult in it. fix: Rewrite the first Safety sentence to hold for both directions of the game: 'Kreston stays out of the hall and at the far end of the room from the pan whichever of you is running it, because a body at full speed in a corridor does not stop for a 16-month-old. Sit him where you can see him from the hall, or use the music on your phone instead of the banging.'

problem: The tray refill landed in Main Event step 1 as reported, but the Afternoon Alternatives were never re-read: bullet 2 is still "Freeze the last of the cocoa milk in the ice tray and check it every twenty minutes." Step 1 now commits BOTH trays to water at 9:15 and puts them back in the freezer "because the afternoon wants them," and the 4:15 row The Ice in the Sink depends on them. The day now has two trays full of water and an afternoon alternative that needs an empty one, so taking that option kills the 4:15 ice the fix was written to save. Prep Tonight and the materials list both say two trays and no more. This is the same block-left-behind failure the round was meant to stop, in the mirror image.
fix: Change the Afternoon Alternatives bullet to freeze the last of the cocoa milk in a cup or on the saucer, not in a tray: "Freeze the last of the cocoa milk in a cup and check it every twenty minutes." Leave step 1 alone.

problem: The Safety block strips the tray for the 4:15 floor session and states the reason as a general fact: "Kreston mouths every tool he reaches at 17 months." The Infant Integration block on the same page still reads "Say the tool names out loud as Azlyn tests them and he takes two into his mouth and one into his vocabulary," and that happens in the morning, when Prep Tonight has tipped the WHOLE tool drawer into a tray on the table and the Opening Activity has tipped that tray out. So the page now says in one block that he mouths every tool he reaches and in another that he takes two of the day's tools into his mouth while the grater, the peeler and the can opener are out. The fix covers 4:15 and leaves 8:00 to 10:15 uncovered.
fix: Either extend the new Safety sentence to the morning line-up ("The sharp tools stay out of the line-up too while he is in the room") or rewrite the Infant Integration clause to name what he is allowed: "...as Azlyn tests them, and hand him the wooden spoon and the lid to mouth while the sharp ones stay up on the table."

problem: The fix landed but the sentence broke its own subject. Step 5 reads: "hand her the watering can and rain from one spot only, standing in the open with the can held high, so the water falls where it would fall." The original said "let her rain," the queue's proposed fix said "holding the can high." As written, you hand her the can and then the imperative tells YOU to rain, and "with the can held high" is a passive participle, which the house style bans.
fix: Rewrite step 5 as: "If the sky stays dry, hand her the watering can and let her rain from one spot only, standing in the open and holding the can high, so the water falls where it would fall. Count to five, then walk her round to read all three."

problem: The new Safety sentence names bottle caps as the first thing to pull out of the bands, but Get Outside still says "Blue may have to be a bottle cap" and Second Main Event step 4 still says "Tip the walk finds in and let her place each one." The page now instructs her to lay the blue find in the line and instructs you to take it straight back out, and nothing tells her what blue becomes after the sweep.
fix: Add a clause to the Safety sentence: "...bottle caps, beads, coins, small blocks and marker lids, and swap her blue cap for something she cannot swallow before he sits down." Leave Get Outside and step 4 as they are.

problem: The Safety block now says "you check the floor before Kreston is loose in the room," but the Infant Integration block on the same page keeps him loose in the room for the whole Main Event: "give him the second cloth and a low cupboard door to wipe while Azlyn does her drawer." Step 4 (the hook, screws or pads) sits inside that stretch. Only the trailing "Use the adhesive pads if he is in the kitchen with you" resolves it, and the infant block never points at the pads, so the two blocks read against each other on first pass.
fix: Add the pointer to the Infant Integration block: "...while Azlyn does her drawer, which is the day the adhesive pads are for." No change to step 4 or the Safety block.

problem: The new Safety sentence establishes that the fence and the stroller handle sit inside Kreston's reach, and then covers only the windsock string and the ribbon. Two other blocks leave brass-fastener pinwheels in exactly those two places: Second Main Event step 7, "Tape one to the fence by the windsock," and Afternoon Alternatives bullet 1, "One pinwheel taped to the stroller handle, and out for a walk." problem: The 4:15 row now reads "Quiet Play: More Symbols on the Spare Cards," but no block on the page makes spare cards. problem: The new Safety sentence and Main Event step 6 contradict each other in the file. Safety now reads "Keep the flour to the one stretch of kitchen floor you can see across... and sweep it up the moment the story is told, because a floured floor is slick under new walkers." Step 6 still reads "Let her lay a fresh trail across the hall after Kreston is in bed, for Joseph to find tonight." That puts flour outside the one permitted stretch, in the hall, and nothing on the page sweeps it. Kreston is put down after it goes down, so the first person to walk the floured hall is the 18-month-old at breakfast, which is the exact hazard the Safety sentence names. The repairer's own report claims the two were reconciled; they were not.
fix: Extend the Safety sentence to cover the evening trail: after "...slick under new walkers," add "The hall trail goes down after Kreston is in bed and comes up before he is out of his room in the morning, so he never walks on it." Leave step 6, the Second Main Event opener and the Infant Integration line as they stand.

problem: The step 7 rewrite drops the containment the finding required and restores the original defect in weaker words. It now reads "Two coins go back out for a turn of her own while Kreston is still up, and both come back into the basket before you put him down." Read plainly, "still up" means still awake and "before you put him down" means bedtime, so two foil-wrapped coins sit out at her height through the whole afternoon with a walking, climbing, mouthing 18-month-old loose in the room. Nothing on the page contains him during 1:00-2:30: step 4 has already let him loose with his bag. Safety ("count them out and count them back into the basket") and Kreston's Afternoon ("The foil coins are not for him, so run his round first and sweep before he is down") both still say the coins are cleared, so the step contradicts two blocks.
fix: Step 7: "Everything into the basket, counted against her map. Two coins go back out for a turn of her own while Kreston is in the high chair, and both come back into the basket before he is loose in the room again." No other block needs touching; the renamed Quiet Play row is fine.

problem: The Safety addition landed but ends "and the loose candy wrappers go back on the table with them." Infant Integration on the same page reads "Keep him at the table end while the cutting happens." The fix therefore moves a choking hazard off the floor and onto the one surface the page parks an 18-month-old beside, with no reach clause anywhere.
